reason: The named contract exercises fresh and replacement workloads for every metric, validates cache and workload limits, and forces cache pressure. Residual zero-count lines are validation errors, tracing fields, and async continuation regions around asserted outcomes.

The named contracts exercise legacy metadata validation and transcoding plus facade reads, writes, cache admission and eviction, canonical and corrupt row decoding, cleanup, and injected failure boundaries. LLVM retains zero-count continuation regions for generic async metric instantiations even though each surrounding outcome is asserted.

The named contract runs two concurrent retirements of one leased Ready entry and proves both converge on Closed. Depending on wake ordering, the losing retirement observes Closed in the drain loop or at this equivalent post-drain recheck.

The named contract reads SimHash rows from resident memory, storage fallback, missing rows, and corrupt rows while asserting request, byte, and timing measurements. LLVM retains a zero-count continuation region for the successful timed ordered-read await.

The named contract forces every measured read and write boundary to success, exercises missing metadata, stale and missing rows, empty outcomes, layer 0 and upper-layer repair, diversity pruning, reciprocal cleanup, build-session reuse and recovery, and flush retry. The residual zero-count lines are tracing fields, async continuation mappings, and generic metric instantiations whose semantic outcomes are asserted.

The named contracts exercise collecting, flushing, preparing, publishing, cache-pressure, and closed-state vector mutation transitions. Residual zero-count lines are invariant failures, tracing fields, and async continuation regions around asserted outcomes.
The named contract exercises deterministic benchmark randomness for every vector metric and both workload shapes. LLVM retains the residual modulo closing edge.

The named contract attaches a generation-matched managed cache, proves snapshot visibility and storage fallback, and holds the lease for the request. LLVM maps the successful generic attachment continuation to this residual zero-count line.

The named contracts exercise exact and filtered search for every metric, directory and directoryless bridge routing, missing companion-row corruption, every explicit budget termination, and writer-scoped stable request views. The residual zero-count lines are async continuation and closing-edge mappings around those asserted operations, plus the index and elapsed-time fields of the search_restricted debug event: the contract runs a search through that deployed entry point under the coverage subscriber, and LLVM leaves those tracing field expressions at zero like the fields at hnsw/search.rs 181 and 182.

The named contract covers missing and repaired entry points, cached-neighbor reuse, sampling accounting, canonical vector batch reads, neighbor prefetch, budget subtraction, upper-layer greedy traversal, and observed versus result-only dispatch. The remaining zero-count lines are tracing fields, closing edges, and LLVM continuation regions for generic async and const-generic instantiations whose outcomes are asserted.

NEON selection and scalar fallback are mutually exclusive runtime or target-feature paths. The architecture matrix runs the production contracts on aarch64 and x86_64 and explicitly forces scalar and native target features.

The named contract runs successful, malformed, row-limited, byte-limited, and cursor-resumed legacy, directory-validation, canonical-backfill, and cleanup scans, including foreign-prefix isolation. LLVM retains zero-count async continuation regions on the exercised scan-prefix awaits.

The named contract fails a target's payload scan and asserts the target is skipped, counted as failed, and charged the hot lane it already read. The zero-count line is a tracing field of the skip warning, which is evaluated only when a warn-level subscriber is installed.

The named contract fails warm scans as they open and asserts the skip, the failure count, and the partial charge. A row read that fails partway through a range returns the same RangeEnd::Failed with the bytes read so far; failing an open SlateDB iterator between rows needs an object-store fault beneath SlateDB, which no current fixture injects.
